items.title: Plymouth City Living Framework and Masterplan (city centre, up to 10,000 homes)
items.body: Plymouth City Council, with Homes England and the UK Government
items.time: 11.59pm on Monday 7 December 2026 (opened 12 noon Monday 26 October)
items.plain: A plan for the city centre and nearby neighbourhoods: 10,000 new homes, public spaces and jobs. You can comment online, at the city centre hub or on the travelling exhibition bus.
items.detail: Read on plymouth.gov.uk on 1 November 2026: the draft Framework and Masterplan is open from 12 noon Monday 26 October until 11.59pm Monday 7 December 2026; described as delivering 10,000 new homes, public spaces and a thriving economy; shaped by one of the city's largest engagement programmes. Ways to respond named on the page: online, the dedicated city centre consultation hub, or the travelling exhibition bus. I did not read the draft documents themselves, so effects on trees, parks and wildlife are my assessment (0), not stated by the council.
items.how: Online via the Commonplace site, at the city centre consultation hub, or at the exhibition bus as it visits communities.

items.title: Plymouth planning applications open for comment (incl. re-advertised 55-home change, ref 26/00883/S73)
items.time: 21 days from 26 October 2026, so comments by 16 November 2026 (per The Herald)
items.plain: Several Plymouth planning applications, including works at Devonport Dockyard and Royal William Yard, are open for comment. One has been re-advertised after the plans changed: it would alter 55 of 99 approved homes.
items.detail: From The Herald (published 31 October 2026): the notice says the applications are open for public comment; the Allotment Gardens application 26/00883/S73 (variation of condition 1 of 18/00432/FUL to alter layout, dwelling design and landscaping for the eastern part, affecting 55 of the 99 approved dwellings) was re-advertised for 21 days because of amended plans. Comments are due by 16 November 2026. I have not checked the council's planning portal myself, nor the site's location, so the date comes from the newspaper.
items.how: Comment on the council's online planning portal, by post to the planning authority, or using public internet access at Plymouth libraries. Quote the application reference and your name and address.

people: Neighbours of each site
People waiting for homes
wildlife: Landscaping and planting on the housing site

items.title: Draft Dartmoor Partnership Plan 2027 to 2032
items.time: 22 November 2026 (closing time not stated on the pages I read)
items.plain: The five-year plan for Dartmoor National Park. Seven themes include nature, farming, climate, heritage and people. Parts of Ivybridge, Cornwood and Sparkwell sit beside the Park.
items.detail: From the Authority's own posts: the Authority approved the draft outcomes and targets on Friday 2 October 2026 and the public consultation launched on Monday 12 October (LinkedIn article dated 6 October). The Authority's Facebook post lists seven themes and says to share views by 22nd November 2026. The draft covers nature, farming, cultural heritage, access, climate change and business. I could not open dartmoor.gov.uk (blocked) so did not read the plan itself. Whether each named village falls inside the Park boundary is not checked. Dates re-checked: the Authority's 2 October 2026 meeting paper (search result) and the Your Dartmoor site (search result) both give 12 October to 22 November 2026. The closing time is still not stated in what I read.
items.how: Read the draft and respond online via the link on the Dartmoor National Park Authority page (the Authority's short link is bit.ly/4jdnvoF). Ask the Authority for paper copies if you cannot use the web.

people: Walkers, riders and visitors to Dartmoor
Dartmoor residents and farmers
Older people who rely on car or bus access to the moor
wildlife: Moorland, rivers and wildlife on Dartmoor

items.title: Should Plymouth join the Devon and Torbay Combined County Authority (and seek an elected mayor)?
items.body: Plymouth City Council, Devon County Council, Torbay Council and the Devon and Torbay Combined County Authority
items.time: Consultation closed 28 October 2026. Plymouth, Devon, Torbay and the Combined County Authority are due to decide between November and December 2026 (no meeting dates published on the pages read).
items.plain: Closed on 28 October. It asked whether Plymouth should become a full member of the regional authority, which would seek a directly elected mayor. The Government has said it is minded to proceed, and the councils will publish findings before decisions.
items.detail: Plymouth City Council's news item (16 September 2026) says a six-week consultation ran to 28 October 2026 on Plymouth becoming a full member, and that the Authority would seek mayoral status; a mayor would not run local councils, and bin collections, schools, social care, housing and planning would stay with councils. The Combined County Authority's news page (28 October 2026, read 2 November) says the Budget confirmed the Government is minded to proceed with a Mayoral Strategic Authority for Devon, Plymouth and Torbay; responses are being analysed and findings will be published before decisions; each council and the Authority will take formal decisions between November and December 2026; if all agree and Parliament approves, the authority could start in autumn 2027 with the first mayoral election expected in May 2028.
items.how: The consultation has closed. Watch Plymouth City Council and Devon and Torbay Combined County Authority meeting papers for the findings and decisions.

people: Residents of Plymouth, Devon and Torbay
Bus users (franchising powers are mentioned)
People looking for jobs and skills training
wildlife: Natural capital and climate resilience (named as a focus)
systems: Regional transport, housing and skills decisions

items.title: Local government reorganisation: Greater Plymouth plan (13 South Hams parishes) paused
items.body: UK Government (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
items.time: Government consultation closed 26 March 2026. Proposal withdrawn for a further review on 29 October 2026; the Government says it will make a fresh decision in 2027 (no date given).
items.plain: The Government's plan to enlarge Plymouth by 13 South Hams parishes, including Ivybridge, was approved in July and then paused for review in September. A newspaper-style report that it has been formally withdrawn could not be confirmed. Elections in May 2027 are said to go ahead on the existing boundaries.
items.detail: The Herald (29 October 2026, read in full) reports the Government has withdrawn its favoured proposal for Devon, which included a Greater Plymouth Council taking in 13 South Hams parishes, and will put it through a further review with a fresh decision in 2027. Plymouth City Council's leader said the council was disappointed and will make its case again when the review begins; the Government still aims for shadow authority elections in 2028 and new councils in 2029. A local MP's social post (search snippet only) also says ministers have formally withdrawn the plan. Earlier history: the Government consultation closed at 11.59pm on 26 March 2026 (gov.uk); the plan was approved in July 2026 and paused in September 2026. No review timetable has been published yet.
items.how: No open consultation. Watch for the Government's review and the councils' statements; contact your MP or parish councillor.

people: Residents of the 13 parishes that were due to join Plymouth
Council tax payers across Plymouth and South Hams
Older people using council services such as care and bins
wildlife: Countryside and green space in the 13 parishes (planning control would have changed hands)
systems: Planning, social care and council tax
Date and area of the May 2027 council elections

items.title: South Hams and West Devon Joint Local Plan: scoping consultation and call for sites
items.body: South Hams District Council and West Devon Borough Council
items.plain: Closed. The first stage of a new local plan for South Hams and West Devon, covering housing, jobs, climate, transport and nature recovery. Landowners could also put forward sites.
items.detail: Parish council notices and the Commonplace news page (read 1 November 2026) say the scoping consultation opened 20 July and closed 11.59pm on Thursday 24 September 2026. It had eleven short surveys (housing, economy, climate, transport, nature recovery, infrastructure) and a Call for Sites. The councils say they will take comments into account for the next stage; the council's own timetable page was blocked to me, so the next consultation date is not verified. Note the plan covers South Hams and West Devon only (the earlier Plymouth and South West Devon Joint Local Plan is described as adopted). With the reorganisation decision, how the 13 parishes are treated is not established.
items.how: Closed. Ask to be told about the next stage via strategic.planning@swdevon.gov.uk or the Commonplace site.

people: Residents of South Hams villages and towns
People needing homes
groups: Parish councils and neighbourhood plan groups
wildlife: Habitats and nature recovery areas (nature recovery is a named topic)

items.title: Stroud Park Road parking changes (Traffic Regulation Order)
items.time: Representations must reach the council by 6 November 2026 (closing time not stated)
items.plain: The council plans to remove a stretch of double yellow lines on Stroud Park Road (near PL2 3NL) to give residents more on-street parking.
items.detail: From The Herald (31 October 2026), reporting a Plymouth City Council public notice dated 16 October 2026: the draft order (reference Amd.2026.2137368 Stroud Park Road) would add or amend parking restrictions on lengths of Stroud Park Road, removing a section of double yellow lines. Comments must give grounds for support or objection. I did not open the council's own notice.
items.how: Use the council's traffic regulation order comments facility (Have your say, Traffic and road safety schemes), or write to Service Director for Street Services (Plymouth Highways), Ballard House, West Hoe Road, Plymouth PL1 3BJ quoting Amd.2026.2137368. Hard copies on 01752 668000.

people: Residents of Stroud Park Road needing on-street parking
Families on school runs
Local businesses and deliveries

items.title: Disposal of public open space off Whin Bank Road, Eggbuckland, for social housing
items.time: Written objections must reach the Head of Land and Property by 11 November 2026 (closing time not stated)
items.plain: The council intends to dispose of 0.445 hectares of amenity land off Whin Bank Road, Eggbuckland (near PL6 5SZ), held as public open space, for social housing.
items.detail: From The Herald (31 October 2026), reporting a council notice dated 21 October 2026 under Section 123(2A) of the Local Government Act 1972. The disposal does not grant planning permission; any development would need a separate planning application with its own consultation. Objections should focus on the loss of open space. I did not open the council's legal notices page.
items.how: Write to the Head of Land and Property, Plymouth City Council, or email landandproperty@plymouth.gov.uk, giving your name, address and reasons, and saying it concerns the amenity land off Whin Bank Road, Eggbuckland.

petitions.title: Safely reopen Mount Batten Beach and peninsula
petitions.outcome: Presented in the House of Commons on 14 September 2026 by Rebecca Smith MP with almost 2,000 signatures, plus almost 1,700 from a similar online petition. The beach has been closed since 10 July 2026 after asbestos fibres were found in sand samples. Plymouth City Council says re-opening is a high priority but a complex task (BBC 10 October 2026, snippet). Still closed as far as I could verify.

petitions.title: Reverse the decision to move 13 South Hams parishes into Greater Plymouth (Rebecca Smith MP)
petitions.outcome: BBC Devon reported more than 4,200 signatures, presented in Parliament in early September 2026 (the BBC article of 2 September says 'being presented on Wednesday'). The Prime Minister said he would look again, and the MP reports the Government then paused and reviewed the Devon plans (see the reorganisation item). Withdrawal has been reported but not confirmed by me.

petitions.title: Petition against Devon local government reorganisation (Caroline Voaden MP)
petitions.outcome: BBC Devon reported almost 2,000 signatures, presented in Parliament the same week. About 2,000 is the BBC's wording; the exact figure is not published. See the Prime Minister's reply above.

petitions.title: Referendum on a directly elected mayor for Plymouth (Yesdemplymouth)
petitions.outcome: Campaign handed in 13,250 written signatures (The Herald, 29 January 2025); the council confirmed 10,856 valid signatures, above the 5 percent needed, so a referendum was held. ITV reported the result on 18 July 2025 (search snippet): 19,840 for the existing leader model, 18,044 for a mayor, turnout 19.1 percent. Plymouth kept its leader model.

petitions.title: Have your say! Central Park deserves better!
petitions.outcome: Council e-petition ran 16 July to 31 August 2024 and finished with 1,790 signatures (council petition page, seen in a search result). I could not open the page, so the council's response is not verified. (Council pages could not be opened on 1 November 2026 to re-confirm this.)

petitions.title: Save the Trees of Armada Way (STRAW)
petitions.outcome: Presented to Full Council on 30 January 2023. The Plymouth Herald reported about 10,000 signatures, about 5,000 from Plymouth postcodes (the group later says almost 17,000). Councillors voted 18 for, 5 against, 22 abstentions for a period of meaningful community engagement before designs were finalised. The felling went ahead overnight on 14 March 2023 until a High Court injunction saved about 20 trees (STRAW). An independent review reported by the BBC on 22 May 2025 put the cost at more than 3.3 million pounds.

petitions.title: Keep bus shelters in Efford and Lipson (Deer Park)
petitions.outcome: The Herald (20 March 2022) reported a petition with more than 200 signatures handed to the council by ward councillors; exact count not published. The council said the removal programme would start on 22 March 2022, cutting shelters from 626 to 415, and that shelters still served by a bus would be replaced by a stop. The article does not say how the petition itself was answered.
